turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Hi everyone. Camille, can you hear me okay? My headset's been acting up all morning.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: I can hear you fine, Dashiell. Zbigniew, Keziah, are you both on?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, I'm here.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Here too. I'm walking back from lunch, so tell me if it gets noisy.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: No problem, Keziah. So for the notes, we have Dashiell Prewitt, Zbigniew Kowalczyk from solutions, Keziah Ashdown from legal, and me. Dashiell, you got the email from Acme last night. Can you give us the short version?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Sure. So Hamish Dunleavy, he's the buyer at Acme, wrote to me last night. He says they've had three export failures in five weeks and won't renew unless something changes. And the last line says Nimbus has offered the same thing for twenty percent less.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Twenty percent. Wow.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Yeah. And the renewal is the end of next month.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Is he bluffing about Nimbus, do you think?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Honestly? Half. I'm sure they got a Nimbus quote. I don't think Hamish wants to migrate in four weeks. But he's angry, and he's got a point.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Right. Zbigniew, before we talk about money, what actually happened with the exports?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: So all three failures have the same cause. Acme has our biggest data set in that region, about four hundred million rows, and the nightly export has a fixed timeout of two hours. Since September their volume pushes it past the timeout on busy nights. The job gets killed, nothing retries it, and their finance team finds an empty file in the morning. The real fix is to split the export into chunks and retry each one.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: And how long does the real fix take?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Two sprints, so about four weeks, if I can borrow one more engineer.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Four weeks lands right on the renewal date, Zbigniew.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: I know. I could have a first version in two weeks, but I wouldn't promise it.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Camille, can I come in here? Please don't put any fix date in the renewal contract. If it's in the agreement and we miss it, Acme can treat that as a breach.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Keziah, with respect, Hamish isn't going to sign anything without a date. That's the whole point of his email.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: I get that. But a date in an email from Zbigniew is a plan. A date in the contract is a promise with a penalty attached.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, let's park that. Keziah, what does the current contract say about outages?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: There's a service level clause. Below ninety-nine percent availability in a month, they get five percent of the monthly fee back. So they might already be owed something. I'm just not sure a failed export counts as unavailability.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: It probably does. The export is listed as a core feature in their order form.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Then they're probably owed credits for September and October already.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Which nobody has offered them.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: No. Which is a bit embarrassing.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: It is. Okay, Dashiell, what were you planning to propose?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: A fifteen percent discount on the renewal. It doesn't match Nimbus, but it shows we're serious.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: I'm not comfortable with that. A fifteen percent cut means paying for one bug with three years of revenue. And next time something breaks, Hamish will ask for another fifteen.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: But Camille, if we lose Acme, we lose a hundred and eighty thousand euros a year. Fifteen percent of that is twenty-seven thousand. That's cheap.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: It's cheap if it keeps them. But I don't think price is the real problem. He's angry because the exports broke and nobody told him why.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: He's angry about both, honestly.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Sorry, go ahead, Dashiell.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: No, I just think if we turn up with an apology and a plan, Hamish takes it to his finance director, who looks at the Nimbus quote, and that's it. He's not just upset, he's counting.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: What if it's not a discount but credits? The ones Keziah mentioned, plus something on top.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: That's much easier for me. Credits are tied to what happened. A discount changes the price for the whole term.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: I like that, Zbigniew. Dashiell, would Hamish accept credits?

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Depends on the size. If it's two thousand euros, he'll laugh at us.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: What about a goodwill credit of ten percent of the annual fee, in the first year of the renewal? Eighteen thousand. Plus what he's already owed.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Eighteen thousand, plus September and October. That's closer. I still think he'll push for a lower price.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Then let him push, and we talk again. But we don't open with a discount.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Okay. I don't love it, but okay.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: And the letter will say goodwill gesture, not an admission that we breached anything.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Of course, Keziah.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Zbigniew, can we also make sure this never fails silently again?

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Yes, easy. We alert their operations team and ours if the export hasn't finished by six in the morning. I can switch that on this week.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Great. Do that first. That's the part Hamish Dunleavy will actually notice.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Should we offer him a call with Zbigniew? He asked for Kowalczyk by name last time.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Sure, happy to.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Okay, let me sum up. No discount. We offer the credits Acme is owed for September and October, plus a goodwill credit of ten percent of the annual fee in the first year. Zbigniew writes a remediation plan with a target date, and the date stays in the plan, not the contract.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Yes. Thank you.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Actions. Zbigniew, the export alerts switched on by Friday, and the written remediation plan to me and Dashiell by Wednesday.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Wednesday's fine. The alerts maybe sooner.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Keziah, can you confirm whether failed exports count under the service level clause, and draft the credit letter by Thursday?

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: Thursday works. I'll send it to you and Dashiell and copy Zbigniew for the technical wording.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Dashiell, you call Hamish tomorrow morning. No numbers. Tell him we've found the cause, we're switching on alerts, and we'd like to meet next Tuesday.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Tomorrow morning, no numbers, meeting on Tuesday. Got it. Do you want to be in that meeting, Camille?

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Yes, put me in. And Zbigniew too.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Sure.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: And if he brings up Nimbus again?

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Then you say we'd like to show him the plan first. Don't argue about Nimbus. We win this on the fix, or not at all.

turns.speaker: c
turns.text: One last thing. Dashiell, nothing about credits in writing until I've sent the letter. Not even a friendly email.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Understood, Keziah. Nothing in writing.

turns.speaker: me
turns.text: Good. Anything else? Then thanks, everyone. Let's speak again Thursday once Keziah's letter is out.

turns.speaker: b
turns.text: Thanks, Camille. Bye.

turns.speaker: a
turns.text: Bye, all.
